content.title: About
content.content: Coffee creamer powder is a dry blend designed to enhance the flavor and texture of coffee. It typically contains vegetable or dairy fats, sweeteners, flavorings, and sometimes added nutrients such as vitamins or minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Powdered creamer is convenient: just add it to a hot beverage and stir.
It is widely used in offices and cafés where fresh dairy products are not practical.
A broad range of flavors exists: classic vanilla, caramel, hazelnut, and lactose‑free options.
Some brands fortify the creamer with probiotics or collagen for extra benefits.
Low moisture content gives it a long shelf life.

items.title: Improves coffee taste
items.content: Creamer makes coffee smoother and sweeter, reducing bitterness.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides carbohydrates and fats that quickly supply energy.

items.title: Vitamin enrichment
items.content: Certain formulas contain B‑vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: May include prebiotic fibers that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Most powdered creamers are plant‑based and suitable for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some creamers contain added sugars, which can be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Ingredients may include nuts, soy, or dairy proteins that can trigger allergies.

items.title: Extra calories
items.content: Because creamers add fats and carbs, excessive use can increase the caloric load of the drink.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Formulas using artificial sweeteners may cause discomfort in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add 1–2 teaspoons of powder to hot coffee and stir until fully dissolved. Adjust the amount to achieve the desired sweetness and creaminess.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container to prevent moisture ingress. For extended storage, keep the package in the refrigerator.
